reasoning.text:
[p0 | acting_agent | action_plan]
2x2 analogy puzzle; only click is interactive. Probe click semantics: BR ring tile (38,38), BR center glyph (46,46), and an unframed TL red tile (14,4) to learn whether outer tiles toggle color, glyphs change, and whether non-framed panels are interactive.

[p1 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Center glyph encodes the ring (gray=blue, white=red). BR glyph requires red at left column + right-mid: R B B / R . R / R B B. (0,0) already red; click (1,0),(1,2),(2,0) to turn them red, matching the glyph to solve.

[p2 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Same glyph->ring rule as L1, palette now blue/orange (top-right swatch). Two glyphs at grid (1,1)&(3,1) dictate 7 tiles must turn orange; click those 7 blue tiles to toggle them orange and satisfy both rings.

[p3 | acting_agent | action_plan]
L3 palette red/orange. Generalized glyph rule: white->center color, gray->other palette color. 14 red tiles must become orange (no conflicts). First batch of 7 clicks to confirm the red->orange toggle, remaining 7 next round.

[s0 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=1 engine=0 accuracy=100.0

[p4 | acting_agent | action_plan]
First 7 clicks confirmed red->orange toggle. Apply remaining toggles so every glyph ring matches (white->center color, gray->other). This should complete L3.

[s1 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=2 engine=1 accuracy=100.0

[p5 | acting_agent | action_plan]
L4 has a 3-color swatch (blue/red/orange) and a blue-marker glyph that makes the old 2-palette rule conflict. Probe the click cycle: single click on a blue tile (22,16) to see whether it becomes orange (2-state) or red (3-state intermediate) before committing a solve.

[s2 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=3 engine=1 accuracy=100.0

[p6 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Click cycles blue->red->orange (3-state, per swatch). Confirm red->orange by clicking already-red (0,1)->orange, and advance (2,1) blue->red->orange. Rule: white->marker, gray->blue; targets orange at (0,1),(2,1),(4,1),(4,2),(4,3).

[p7 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Cycle blue->red->orange confirmed; (0,1),(2,1) now orange. Finish glyph(3,2)s ring: make (4,1),(4,2),(4,3) orange via two clicks each (blue->red->orange). Completes all 3 glyph dictates -> should solve L4.

[s3 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=4 engine=2 accuracy=100.0

[p8 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Unified rule: glyph white->tile MUST equal marker; gray->tile MUST NOT equal marker. Current all-orange-target config failed because glyph(1,3) blue-marker gray tiles were still blue. Set forced tiles (mostly ->red) to satisfy all != constraints; minimal clicks.

[p9 | acting_agent | action_plan]
L5 same constraint logic, richer glyph skins: EQ={white,pink}, NEQ={gray,green-block}, color3=non-tile placeholder. Derived from 22 overlapping tiles with zero conflicts. 9 tiles must become purple (green->purple, 1 click each); rest stay green.

[s4 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=5 engine=3 accuracy=100.0

[p10 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Constraint-satisfaction goal falsified (9-purple checkerboard gives reward 0). Trace the click cycle length on one green tile (8,22): does green->purple->green (2-cycle) or is there a hidden 3rd tile color (e.g. pink6) the target needs? Fundamental re-probe before expensive full-config experiments.

[s5 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=6 engine=4 accuracy=100.0

[p11 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Cycle=2 confirmed; glyph-constraint goal exhausted as insufficient. Probe untested interactions: click two glyph centers (3,4)=(40,30) and checker (1,2)=(24,14), and the swatch (55,2). If glyphs/swatch are clickable in L5 (unlike L1-4), that reveals the missing mechanic.

[p12 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Characterize new glyph-click mechanic: re-click checker(1,2) marker (24,14) to test if plus-toggle reverses; click checker(3,2) marker (24,30) for 2nd confirmation; click classic glyph(4,2) MARKER center (24,38) to confirm classic glyphs inert.

[p13 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Test whether the L5 win is all 3 checker (active) glyph markers turned purple/activated. Current (1,2)=green,(3,2)=purple,(5,4)=green; click checker (1,2) at (24,14) and (5,4) at (40,46) to make all three purple. Cheap, high-information probe of the operator-activation goal hypothesis.

[s6 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=7 engine=5 accuracy=100.0

[p14 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Test H1: the intended L5 solution may be simply finding and clicking the 3 hidden checker operators. RESET to clean all-green L5, then click operators (1,2)=(24,14), (3,2)=(24,30), (5,4)=(40,46) once each. This activates all 3 (markers purple) with a clean operator-driven tile pattern, distinct from both failed states. Verify RESET returns clean L5.

[p15 | acting_agent | action_plan]
H1 was one tile short: (2,2) got double-toggled back to green by operators (1,2)&(3,2). Click (2,2)->purple to complete the state where all 3 checker rings are satisfied with purple markers (edges purple, corners green). Tests whether the L5 win = operators activated + checker rings satisfied.

[p16 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Test: win = all 18 EVEN-parity tiles purple + all checker markers purple (the inverted/complement pattern, reached via operators which is why operators exist). Markers already purple; click the 8 remaining even tiles to purple. Distinct from all prior failed states.

[p17 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Build H2 (classic solution + operators activated). RESET to clean L5, then set the 9 odd-parity classic-solution tiles purple. Next turn: click 3 operators (markers->purple) and revert their even-neighbor side effects, yielding 9-odd-purple + purple checker markers - the only difference from the failed 9-purple being operator activation.

[s7 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=8 engine=6 accuracy=100.0

[p18 | acting_agent | action_plan]
Full CSP re-proven dead (only all-green-markers satisfies, = failed 9-purple). Testing H1: 9-odd-purple classic solution + all 3 operator markers PURPLE (operators activated = mandatory new mechanic), never cleanly tested. From current 9-odd-purple state: stamp 3 checkers (24,14),(24,30),(40,46) to flip markers purple (also flips their even ortho neighbors), then revert those 9 even neighbors to green. Net target: 9 odd tiles purple + 3 purple markers + rest green.

[p19 | acting_agent | action_plan]
L6 = new yellow(11)/green(14) constraint level: 4 classic green-marker glyphs + 22 editable yellow tiles (each with a NEW unexplained pink top-center dot). Unique constraint solution = 12 tiles green, 10 yellow. Probe 3 of the needed-green tiles (1,0),(2,2),(4,6) to confirm tiles toggle yellow->green and observe pink-dot behavior before committing the remaining 9 clicks.

[s8 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=9 engine=7 accuracy=100.0

[p20 | acting_agent | action_plan]
L6 EQ-up confirmed = transition coupler (click flips tile + editable tile above), not a goal constraint (combined glyph+vertical-equality CSP is infeasible). Goal = glyph-only constraint target (12 green/10 yellow), L1-L4 regime. Solved the per-column GF(2) click system from current board: 10 clicks reach the target (simulation-verified, order-independent XOR). Committing full solution to attempt the win.

[s9 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=10 engine=8 accuracy=100.0

[s10 | synthesizer | world_model_version]
round=11 engine=9 accuracy=100.0
